body: AI systems are making rapid progress in mathematics, but this progress is hard to measure. Benchmarks of solved problems saturate, and in benchmarks of open problems each problem can be resolved for the first time only once. We present SqueezeBench, a benchmark that is resilient to saturation: a success raises the bar instead of removing the problem. Each problem fixes an integer function f(n) whose values are known only for small n, and the benchmark keeps a lower and an upper record on it. A record is a computable Lean function with a machine-checked proof that it bounds f. A submission proposes a new function and proves that it bounds f, that it is no worse than the current record at any n, and that it is strictly better at some n. Once accepted, it becomes the record that the next submission has to beat. The system thus chooses the bound as well as its proof, and it may improve the record at a single n or its growth rate. At every n, the gap between the two records shows how far the certified bounds are from determining f(n). Every proof is checked by two independent Lean kernels, so no referee needs to check the mathematics. The checks also reject a function that computes f by exhaustive search at small n, and a maintainer only reads the submitter's report and looks for such a search at larger n. We release ten problems from extremal combinatorics with twenty proved initial records and the admission tools. As a baseline, agents based on a frontier language model, with at most one hour per record, had 82 submissions accepted and improved every record, without going beyond the published literature. Agents based on two newer models then started from these records, had 60 more submissions accepted and improved 19 of the 20 records again. For eight of the ten problems, at least one record is still asymptotically behind the best published bound.

summaryZh: 本文提出了SqueezeBench，这是一个旨在解决数学基准测试饱和问题的评估框架。不同于传统的静态问题集，SqueezeBench通过要求模型不断改进对整数函数f(n)的边界证明来提升难度。所有提交的证明均通过Lean内核进行机器验证，确保了结果的客观性。该基准测试不仅能衡量模型的数学推理能力，还能通过不断更新的记录保持评估的有效性。实验表明，该框架能有效区分不同代际模型的数学能力，为数学推理研究提供了持续的挑战。
